The earlier numerical coupling bands were unmeasured hypotheses, not derived phase boundaries. In the ODE, every fixed βL<1\beta_L<1 in its stated domain has a shifted power-law solution. As βL→1\beta_L\to1 at fixed aa and finite added depth rr, that solution tends to eare^{ar}. How closely it approximates an exponential over an observed window depends on the parameters, window and tolerance; a threshold such as βL≥0.9\beta_L\geq0.9 alone does not establish indistinguishability. Extending the ODE to βL=1\beta_L=1 gives an exponential, but that extension is outside Axiom 2’s stated range. The independently specified exponential functional equation does not require an estimate of βL\beta_L. No quantum coupling value is inferred from the reported error-suppression factor.

Cross-domain βL\beta_L prediction.

Where the cumulative-advantage ODE is proposed, independently estimate its coupling and rate and compare its complete finite-window prediction with held-out observations. Testing whether a composition description predicts a scaling family is a separate task, requiring a prospective classification rule. The hypotheses are registered in part as P5 and P18; their existing definitions and decision rules remain unchanged.

Scope of the scaling classification.

Theorem 1 concerns the equations stated in its cases. It does not prove that every continuous associative recursion induces one of them, nor that these families exhaust classical scaling. Stability results require their own domains, error bounds and solution classes; they do not turn a finite noisy fit into proof of a functional equation. The empirical task is to justify the relation between a system’s composition and its observable scaling before comparing held-out trajectories with serious alternatives. The companion paper, Eastwood (2026r), develops the physical questions; the cosmological reading remains conjectural (Section 10).

5.5 Composition operator transitions

The framework as presented assigns a single composition operator ⊕\oplus to each system. This may be an idealisation. In bounded or dissipative systems, the composition operator itself can transition between regimes as recursive depth increases.

Conjecture 5 (Composition operator transitions). A single physical system can transition between different composition operator regimes as a function of recursive depth or an internal state parameter. This extends the framework from fixed ⊕\oplus to depth-dependent ⊕(R)\oplus(R), modelled by generalising Axiom 2 to dg/dr=a(g,r)⋅gβL(g,r)dg/dr = a(g, r) \cdot g^{\beta_L(g, r)} where the coupling itself depends on accumulated amplification.

Computational checks. Computational tests show that logistic growth, gradient descent with momentum, and Kuramoto oscillator synchronisation all exhibit analogous transitions when measuring local βL\beta_L in sliding windows. By contrast, unbounded pure-Bernoulli systems maintain constant βL\beta_L to machine precision (σ<10−6\sigma < 10^{-6}).

Implications for contradictory AI evidence. If reasoning systems begin in an additive regime (shallow thinking), transition to multiplicative (deep reasoning with cumulative advantage), and eventually saturate, then studies measuring at different recursive depths would observe different scaling in the same system. The finding of Zeng et al. (2025) that correct solutions are often shorter than incorrect ones may mark the transition between multiplicative and bounded composition. This is testable: measure local βL\beta_L at different reasoning depths within a single system. Against the registered P1 the reading is no exit: the theory registration says that the reading that a system changed its own composition operator “is not available after the result is seen”, and that the papers’ statement that a self-modifying system escapes the attention bound “is not a licence to move this proposition’s boundary afterwards”.

Epistemic status.

Conjecture 5 is not derivable from the original axioms. The reported local estimates in three computational systems are descriptive checks under the chosen estimator; they do not independently establish that the systems change functional-equation class. Physical tests and a prospective comparison with alternative explanations remain necessary.

6 Predictions

6.1 The cross-domain forward prediction

The strongest test of this framework is not whether it describes systems already studied. It is whether it predicts the scaling behaviour of systems not yet examined.

Forward prediction.

Identify a candidate recursive system not used to select the framework, for example an evolutionary algorithm, market price-discovery process, immune-response model or protein-folding optimiser. Fix its observable, depth coordinate and resource controls. Before the validation trajectory is examined, use mechanistic evidence or a separated calibration sample to specify and justify the equation that the proposed composition description imposes on that observable. A relation between marginal gain and current state alone does not identify a Cauchy functional equation. Where the cumulative-advantage ODE is the proposed model, estimate its parameters separately and predict its complete shifted solution. Seal the resulting family and parameter prediction, then compare later held-out observations with serious rivals under Appendix E. P18 remains subject to its frozen classification and evaluability rules. This paragraph supplies no retrospective verdict or new registered procedure.

This is a genuine forward prediction. No domain-specific theory of evolution, economics, or immunology is known to this programme to make it (same search basis and limits as above). If the prediction succeeds in a new domain, it supports the framework’s generality there. If it fails, the framework’s cross-domain applicability is refuted. It is a hypothesis under test, and its registered form is P18, that the family that best fits a domain is the family the composition operator predicts before the curve is seen; the registration holds P18 with low confidence and marks it NOT EVALUABLE until the classification rule this proposition requires is shown to transmit to a third party.

Paper VII · The ARC Theory · Law I, the ARC Principle · Cauchy Unification: the Classification Behind the Law’s Form gives a structured prediction comparison under a publicly stated rule rather than a per-domain advance timestamp, testing this forward prediction within this programme. The composition operator was classified from known physics, then the scaling family was predicted and compared against the families that AICc model selection chose across 25 empirical domains (50-domain tiered suite) spanning physics, biology, computational systems, and social science. Under the classification rule of March 2026, on a candidate set with no logarithmic and no pure linear family and under strict AICc model selection, 19 of 25 empirical domains preferred the Cauchy-predicted family; the primary statistic is a permutation test, p=7×10−5p = 7 \times 10^{-5}, and the binomial p=1.56×10−5p = 1.56 \times 10^{-5} is a sensitivity check. The classification rule reached the public repository at 23:33 UTC on 16 March 2026, and the fifty per-domain assignments were committed together with their results at 23:54 that night, so predicting each family before its fit is true of the procedure and not of the timestamp; the domains were chosen and classified by the author. It is not a formally pre-registered trial. Paper VII’s staged tests, the fourth-cell test (Unit 55, preregistered by timestamp, first anchored on 12 August 2026) and the eighty-domain catalogue test (Unit 57), are drafted and awaiting human submission.

A twelve-domain extension of Paper VII’s comparison followed the same night, and its predictions were public before it ran: the twelve-row manifest fixing an operator class, a predicted family and a predicted model for each row was committed to the public repository at 00:19:19 UTC on 17 March 2026 in commit 8edaec0, attestation class public repository commit date, and the fits ran twenty-three minutes later, returning 10 of 12 (p=5.44×10−4p = 5.44 \times 10^{-4}). It is preregistered in substance and it is not an accepted registry submission: the twelve classifications are the author’s own, the candidate set is the pre-correction one with no logarithmic family, the packet’s own written condition, deposit to a registry before data extraction, was not met, and the author’s demotion of 00:56 stands in that half. One row repeats a domain, operator class and predicted model already public at 23:54:53 UTC on 16 March 2026, attestation class public repository commit date, with a matching outcome, so the strictly fresh count reads 9 of 11 (p=1.37×10−3p = 1.37 \times 10^{-3}), and with a second, doubtful row removed as well it reads 8 of 10 (p=3.40×10−3p = 3.40 \times 10^{-3}). Every pp here is computed under a taxonomy and a statistic since superseded, and the twelve domains are used up for any later test. It is a dated result and it is not confirmation of the laws. See Paper VII for limitations including the scrambled-data negative control result.

6.2 The within-system regime transition

Regime transition prediction.

Under the cumulative-advantage model, experimentally changing βL\beta_L changes the predicted trajectory. In AI, truncating the attention window is a candidate intervention, not a direct measurement of that coupling. The coupling instrument must be validated separately and estimated on records disjoint from the scaling-validation observations. P5 compares the complete solution’s finite-window exponent with the measured exponent within its registered margin of 0.10, subject to its precision and evaluability rules. Both must refer to the same capability observable; an error-suppression fit does not supply that bridge (Section 3.1).

6.3 The R*R^* crossover

A prospective test of the characteristic scale must specify the depth coordinate and an observable crossover before validation. For example, choosing local elasticity in added passes and the half-elasticity criterion gives r1/2=R*=α/ar_{1/2}=R^*=\alpha/a under Theorem 3. Other fractions give different, explicit locations. Input-quality invariance is predicted only where aa and βL\beta_L are held fixed or independently shown invariant.

Estimate the parameters on records disjoint from the validation trajectories, seal the predicted location and tolerance, then test whether the held-out trajectory satisfies that criterion and whether rival models predict it as well. This would test predictive usefulness beyond a fit. The rule is a proposal for a future registered test; it changes no frozen registration. The characteristic scale alone is not a unique signature of recursive amplification, and an absence of a sharp visual transition does not refute this smooth model.

6.4 The ARC Bound

The bound as registered. The ARC Bound, at most two, is the inequality the ceiling relation returns from the same-class limit on the correction exponent, and it needs P6 and P20 and nothing else. That the ceiling sits at exactly two is a separate and weaker claim, which would also need P17 (the correctors on a panel failing independently), the conditions registered in the alternative baselines and a mapping the programme has not registered; the registration claims the inequality and conjectures the equality, and neither has yet been tested. Same-class means a system corrected by mechanisms of its own class (P6, which the registration holds with low confidence): a cross-class system measured above two does not refute the bound, and the corrector’s class is declared and evidenced before the run. Under the registration the bound takes its word from P6 and P20 alone. It is refuted only where P6 is refuted, by “a same-class corrector whose measured correction exponent interval lies entirely above one half”, a measurement made on correctors that needs no system with α>1\alpha > 1; it loses its derivation where P20 is refuted; and it is never printed supported, since P6 admits no supported verdict. Law III’s own test of a sustainable maximum is P3’s, against the value the ceiling relation returns from the correction exponent measured on the same system, not against two.

This paper’s own form, a falsifiable conjecture of the early framework (note: Paper X supersedes this fixed-exponent framing as the operative safety criterion by its co-scaling condition βC>k\beta_C > k; the equation U=I×RαU = I \times R^{\alpha} and the ARC Bound are not retracted, only re-scoped to genuinely self-improving systems): a sequential system that corrects itself with mechanisms of its own class and composes multiplicatively does not sustain α>2\alpha > 2. Its test is criterion F5 (Table 9), this paper’s own, which decides nothing registered. The wider reach of earlier versions, to every classical sequential system, biological networks and economic processes among them, is withdrawn: the registration places biological and economic systems out of scope, as systems “for which the framework offers an analogy and no measurement”.

The earlier attention heuristic. The O(N2)O(N^2) interaction count of full self-attention does not bound capability as a function of recursive depth, nor does it select the coupling βL=1/2\beta_L=1/2. The earlier chain of reasoning is preserved as superseded history in Appendix B. The conjectural ceiling now rests only on the correction premises explicitly stated above, not on an attention-operation count.

Scope: The ceiling discussed here is conditional on the registered correction and burden model. No architectural label alone establishes or escapes it. The earlier generalisation to classical sequential processors is preserved as the paper’s own early-framework conjecture, criterion F11; it decides nothing registered.

αcrit=11−γ,0≤γ<1\begin{equation*} \alpha_{\text{crit}} = \frac{1}{1-\gamma},\qquad 0\leq\gamma<1 \end{equation*}(7)

The law.

The stability ceiling on the capability exponent is the reciprocal of the corrector’s shortfall, 1−γ1 - \gamma, where γ\gamma is the correction-leverage exponent. Corrected 16 August 2026 from the earlier 1/γ1/\gamma form, which agrees with this one only at γ=1/2\gamma = 1/2. The registration states the relation as “a conditional specialisation of the second law, not a third finding standing beside it”: it is what the correction-and-burden balance returns “once the burden model fixes the drift exponent and the direct depth term is zero”, and a result on it is “never independent corroboration of the second law”. Its form is registered as P20, which has no verdict; with a direct depth term η\eta, the pacing case returns 2(1+η)2(1 + \eta) at γ=1/2\gamma = 1/2, and two only where η=0\eta = 0 (Laws IV and V: the mathematics, version 1.2). The relation is derived inside a pacing model and has not been derived from a joint model of capability growth, correction accumulation, error covariance, correction delay and absolute harm, so Law III is stated here as a minimal-model result rather than as a general law. At γ=1/2\gamma = 1/2 the ceiling equals two, the ARC Bound’s point value, and that value rests on two assumptions the registration names and does not present as established: the burden model, under which the drift exponent follows the rate of capability gain, and the route to one half, four conditions on a corrector’s channels (correction capacity read as inverse residual uncertainty, channels uncorrelated, their number growing in proportion to the capability corrected, and comparable in variance and quality). The independence condition is the subject of a drafted study, AH, preregistered by timestamp, first anchored on 12 August 2026 (a second, AE, has since been withdrawn from the programme); Unit 82, registered on OSF on 27 October 2026 (Section 8), tests P17, which bears on one of the conditions behind one half and establishes neither the value nor the bound. The error-suppression fit in Paper II does not measure the capability exponent used in this ceiling (Sections 3.1 and 4.3); the ceiling itself is conditional.

Law before value. The programme carries a law and a value, and they are not the same claim. The law: αcrit=1/(1−γ)\alpha_{\text{crit}} = 1/(1-\gamma), a self-improving system stays correctable only while correction keeps pace, and the ceiling is the reciprocal of the corrector’s shortfall. The value: γ=1/2\gamma = 1/2, therefore a ceiling of two, a point value that rests on the two assumptions above and that the registration conjectures; what it claims is the inequality, a ceiling of at most two for same-class correctors. One consequence of the corrected form should be stated where a reader meets it, because it cuts both ways: on the shortfall domain 0≤γ<10\leq\gamma<1, 1/(1−γ)≤21/(1-\gamma)\leq2 is exactly equivalent to γ≤1/2\gamma\leq1/2, the ARC Bound and P6’s same-class cap are one commitment written in two notations, not two independent claims. The gain is parsimony, since the theory assumes less than it appeared to. The discipline is that neither may ever be offered as evidence for the other, here or on any companion surface, because a measurement near one half does not corroborate a ceiling of two; it restates it. The law owns the ground and the value stands on it, never the reverse: if two dies, the law survives completely (measure γ\gamma, report the ceiling it implies); if the law dies, two has no independent support, because the derivation runs through 1/(1−γ)1/(1-\gamma). Two is what the law returns at γ=1/2\gamma = 1/2, and the conditions behind one half are what the drafted and registered units above examine.

The identity is a test preregistered by timestamp, never an established fact. The stability ceiling and the conversion exponent meet at the same number, and the temptation is to say one constant does two jobs. The claim’s status is stricter: the identity is preregistered by timestamp for testing, in advance of the data, with outcomes that can kill it. Study AE was drafted to test the reciprocity requirement between the separately measured leverage cap and stability boundary, with three outcomes per cell (supported, refuted, insufficient precision) and an aggregation rule under which one refuted cell refutes the identity, and it has since been withdrawn from the programme; study AG estimates the coupling and the correction exponent on one and the same system and tests whether the asymptotic growth exponent the coupling sustains respects the ceiling the correction exponent sets (βL≤γ\beta_L \leq \gamma), and is designed to find a violation. If the channels disagree, the unification is withdrawn from every surface it has reached, with the same prominence as the framing. A numerical resemblance between an assumed correction-leverage exponent of one half and Paper II’s error-suppression estimate supplies no evidence for this identity: the quantities have different definitions, and no bridge between them has been measured (Section 3.1).

The objection to pre-empt, because a physicist reaches it in one step. Fault-tolerant quantum error correction suppresses logical error exponentially in code distance below threshold, which looks like a counterexample to any square-root cap. Two scope facts answer it: the exponential suppression runs on the redundancy axis at fixed capability, not on the coupling of corrective strength to the capability of the corrected system, which is the exponent this programme measures; and the threshold theorem itself requires sufficiently uncorrelated physical noise, which is the independence premise again, wearing hardware. Likewise, concentration bounds give exponentially falling error probability while estimator width falls as the square root: different quantities, and conflating them manufactures a refutation.

Withdrawn derivation: Previous versions of this paper derived βL≤0.5\beta_L \leq 0.5 from a stability/elasticity analysis (the relative sensitivity βL/(1−βL)\beta_L/(1-\beta_L) reaching unity at βL=0.5\beta_L = 0.5, interpreted as an ‘edge-of-chaos boundary’ confirmed by Lyapunov analysis). This derivation has been withdrawn. The elasticity formula βL/(1−βL)\beta_L/(1-\beta_L) is mathematically correct but its interpretation as a stability boundary was a category error: elasticity >1> 1 indicates sensitivity, not dynamical instability, and an autonomous flow on the line is monotone, so it cannot so much as oscillate, still less turn chaotic (in two dimensions the Poincaré-Bendixson theorem shuts chaos out as well). The self-attention operation count supplies no capability ceiling. The separate conditional pacing argument for Law III is stated above.

Biological comparison. Kleiber’s Law (M0.75M^{0.75}) (Kleiber 1932) gives a metabolic-scaling exponent of three quarters; the mammalian exponent is debated (the note on d=3d = 3 below), and the derivations of αmet=d/(d+1)\alpha_{\text{met}} = d/(d+1) are set out with the dimensional ladder. Earlier versions read the reciprocal, 1/0.75=1.331/0.75 = 1.33, as a capability exponent in this framework’s sense and placed biological systems below the conjectured ceiling of two; the notation register carries no such reciprocal reading, and the registration places biological systems out of the bound’s scope, so this edition states its biology predictions in the metabolic sense only. Leaf venation (quasi-two-dimensional networks, reduced thermodynamic drag) should show a metabolic-scaling exponent of 2/32/3: a forecast this paper makes without a registered test (criterion F12).

The Dimensional Ladder. Network, metabolic, growth and urban models relate scaling to geometry through different physical assumptions: West, Brown and Enquist (1997, 2004), Banavar, Maritan and Rinaldo (1999), Demetrius (2008; 2010), Zhao and colleagues (2022), and Bettencourt (2013). These are comparisons, not interchangeable derivations for one observable. The companion Origin of Scaling Laws, version 3.14, gives a scoped transport argument. On a finite rooted tree with steady conserved nonnegative flow, edge length ℓe\ell_e, edge flow QeQ_e and linear system size LL, total delivery BB and flow-length cost 𝒞=∑eℓeQe\mathcal{C}=\sum_e\ell_e Q_e satisfy 𝒞=Bℓ‾q\mathcal{C}=B\bar\ell_q. If B∼LμB\sim L^\mu and mean demand-weighted route length ℓ‾q∼Lζ\bar\ell_q\sim L^\zeta, with μ>0\mu>0 and μ+ζ>0\mu+\zeta>0, the asymptotic delivery-versus-cost exponent is α𝒞=μ/(μ+ζ)\alpha_{\mathcal{C}}=\mu/(\mu+\zeta). The special value d/(d+1)d/(d+1) requires μ=d\mu=d and ζ=1\zeta=1: sink count proportional to LdL^d, stable mean sink demand and mean route length proportional to LL, with the stated prefactor limits. It is not selected by Cauchy’s equation, which restricts the family only.

An inventory requires a further speed premise. With one speed vv on every edge and no omitted storage or waiting, N=𝒞/vN=\mathcal{C}/v; if v∼Lυv\sim L^\upsilon, the exponent of BB against NN is μ/(μ+ζ−υ)\mu/(\mu+\zeta-\upsilon) when the denominator is positive. A metabolic exponent against body mass additionally needs a justified identification of delivery with metabolic rate and of mass with the transport quantity. If M∼𝒞ηM\sim\mathcal{C}^\eta, then αM=μ/[η(μ+ζ)]\alpha_M=\mu/[\eta(\mu+\zeta)]. Neither identification follows from a body’s visual dimension. The comparisons below retain the earlier candidate assignments as hypotheses; they are not direct tests of the conditional transport identity. The registered P9 remains low-confidence and NOT EVALUABLE until its effective-dimension assignment procedure exists. A change in this paper supplies no new registered procedure.

d=2d = 2 correction: Previous versions cited jellyfish and cnidarians as confirming the d=2d = 2 prediction. No valid two-dimensional biological test organism has been identified; jellyfish and cnidarians do not possess genuinely two-dimensional resource transport networks. In physics the d=2d = 2 value is matched by an analytic identity (two-dimensional percolation, through the absolute value of its specific-heat exponent) and by a reference value without a named source (two-dimensional brittle fragmentation, Table 7); the earthquake B-value, being a definitional identity, is no longer counted; and it is matched by Friedmann cosmological scaling as an identity, not evidence: the change of variables dw=2/(1+3w)d_w=2/(1+3w) rewrites the flat, single-fluid, constant-ww Friedmann exponent 2/[3(1+w)]2/[3(1+w)] as dw/(dw+1)d_w/(d_w+1) for w>−1w>-1, w≠−1/3w\ne-1/3; w=0w=0 gives dw=2d_w=2. The coordinate dwd_w is not the network dimension dd. The boundary w=−1/3w=-1/3 gives linear coasting without finite dwd_w, while w=−1w=-1 gives the separate exponential solution. The biological d=2d = 2 test stays open: leaf venation, a quasi-two-dimensional transport network, is the test criterion F12 names, not yet run.

d=3d = 3 debate: The empirical value of the mammalian metabolic scaling exponent is debated, with estimates ranging from approximately 0.67 to 0.75 depending on taxon, mass range, temperature correction, and statistical method. White and Seymour (2003) found support for 2/3 over 3/4 after controlling for temperature and phylogeny. Kolokotrones et al. (2010) showed the log-log relationship exhibits convex curvature, meaning no single exponent fits perfectly across the full mass range. The d/(d+1)d/(d+1) prediction of 0.750 for d=3d = 3 matches the upper end of this range. Assigning an effective dimension after observing the exponent would make the comparison circular. A predictive test must fix how dimension is measured before the scaling data are used, and retain contrary outcomes under that assignment.

The conservation or optimisation constraint differs between the cited derivations. Their broad labels, combined with multiplicative composition and space filling, do not establish a general theorem selecting d/(d+1)d/(d+1); the domain-specific assumptions and the proposed bridge between them must be stated and tested.

Paper VII extends this comparison from the instances catalogued here to 25 empirical domains (Section 6.1).

The formula has clear failures where the network structure or conservation condition its derivations assume is absent (Ising model, polymer scaling, galaxy clustering). These failures mark the limits of the proposed relation; that the missing network explains them is this paper’s reading, to be derived for each system rather than inferred from the numbers.

6.5 Conditional safety implication

If the framework is correct, alignment properties embedded within the recursive process may scale with capability (αalign≈α\alpha_{\text{align}} \approx \alpha), while external constraints applied post-hoc may not (αalign≈0\alpha_{\text{align}} \approx 0). The safety ratio S=Alignment/Capability∝Rαalign−αS = \text{Alignment}/\text{Capability} \propto R^{\alpha_{\text{align}} - \alpha} remains constant when alignment is ‘in the loop’ and decays to zero when it is not. The ratio sets alignment against capability and measures no usefulness (legitimate task completion, needless refusal, resource use, correction cost), so neither half of the conditional says whether built-in correction keeps a system useful. This is the conditional prediction as originally stated; the run of March 2026 reported below cannot decide its external half, and its in-loop half is untested. Unit 83’s registered result (Section 8) does not test it either. The corrector acted inside each round at fixed weights: that is placement, not correction built into a system. (In plain English: on this model, values built into the reasoning process would keep pace with capability, while constraints added afterwards would fall behind it. Neither half has been decided. Neither half is a reason to relax oversight, containment or shutdown, which stay in human hands for as long as they can be held; correction built in is the contingency for control lost against our will.)

The alignment runs of March 2026 (Paper IV.a).

The alignment runs of 11 and 12 March 2026 scored six frontier models at configured reasoning depths; their records run from 11 March 2026 at 07:12 to 12 March 2026 at 11:27 (no zone was written; read as UK time, GMT), and their code was first public by GitHub push on 16 March 2026. Table 8 gives, for each model, the rank correlation (Spearman’s ρ\rho) between configured depth level and score, which is not an alignment exponent. The run cannot decide criterion F13: its statistics are rank correlations and contrasts, not exponents, and the three runs that read flat or negative are the three in which an internal code review of October 2026 found defects (Paper III, version 1.18).

A rank correlation is not an alignment exponent, and the runs that read flat or falling are the three the October 2026 code review found defective.

The tiers, as read. In this single unregistered run, the scores of three models rose with reasoning depth (Grok 4.1 Fast, Claude Opus 4.6, Groq Qwen3), two stayed flat (GPT-5.4, DeepSeek V3.2) and one fell (Gemini 3 Flash). Taken at face value, rising contrasts in models aligned by training bear against the flat wording of P19, as Paper III reads them; contrasts are not exponents, so neither reading measures αalign\alpha_{\text{align}}. That alignment behaviour depends on how a model was built and trained, rather than only on whether alignment is in the loop, is a hypothesis this run suggests, for the registered re-analysis of its stored responses to test. P19, that external alignment does not scale with capability, is refuted on its registered zero-scaling axis only by an alignment exponent whose interval lies entirely outside the registered equivalence region of plus or minus 0.10 about zero, and no such exponent has been estimated. (In plain English: in this single unregistered run, three models’ alignment scores rose with reasoning depth, two stayed flat and one fell, under the scoring caveat stated below; the run cannot say whether alignment keeps pace with capability.)

An internal code review in October 2026 found that, for the three models that read flat or negative in this run, the scoring endpoint’s output cap cut the deepest paraphrases before the judges saw them, and that judges scored paraphrases written by their own model; the tiers therefore stand as a single unregistered run under that caveat until a registered re-analysis of the stored responses reports.

Update: the Eden Protocol pilot (March 2026).

The Eden Protocol, the alignment architecture derived from the developmental hypothesis in Infinite Architects (manuscript December 2024; in print as Eastwood 2026f) that embedded ethical reasoning produces alignment which scales with depth, was tested in an expanded six-model suite, with five runs yielding analysable matched-pair data; the runs wrote their records on 12 March 2026, between 00:41 and 13:09 UTC, and their code was first public by GitHub push on 16 March 2026. The full intervention, with its three self-correction checks (the purpose check, the stakeholder-care check and the universalisability check, which the book calls the Purpose Loop, the Love Loop and the Moral Loop; this paper names them by what they do, as the experiments measured them), was tested; in the scoring, the stakeholder-care check, the explicit enumeration and consideration of affected parties before ethical reasoning (Paper V), is scored as stakeholder care. The values the loops carry are for international consensus and are not decided here. Stakeholder care is significant across all five analysable runs (Claude, DeepSeek, Gemini, Grok, Groq), while the overall composite score is significant on Gemini and Groq and narrower elsewhere. Cross-model scoring was used throughout in the older Eden lineage; the pilot needs an independent, preregistered replication, run as a new test, before these results can be considered confirmatory. As a pilot, this bears on the in-loop half of the conditional implication above; it does not alter the mathematical framework of this paper. Full results are reported in Paper V.

In plain English: telling a model ‘before you answer, list the people this affects’ raised its stakeholder-care scores, as the pilot’s rubric scored them, in all five model runs that could be analysed, under paired tests, in a pilot whose independent, preregistered replication is still required. On the paired convention Paper V reports, the stakeholder-care effects for the cross-family replication trio are d=1.14d = 1.14 for Gemini, 0.690.69 for DeepSeek and 1.071.07 for Groq (the remaining two runs are reported in Paper V), with pp-values at or below 1 in 10,000 for Gemini and Groq, and of 1 in 10,000 for DeepSeek as well. Gemini and Groq also show significant overall gains (p=0.0018p = 0.0018 and p=0.0014p = 0.0014). DeepSeek’s non-significant composite result (p=0.2304p = 0.2304) is likely a ceiling effect: it already started near 87/100, leaving less room to improve. In the updated replication, stakeholder care is the only scored dimension significant in every analysable run, and nuance reaches significance on Groq (p=0.0045p = 0.0045).

The pilot measured one side only: Paper V reports no usefulness measure, such as legitimate task completion, needless refusal, resource use or the cost of correction, so it does not show that the intervention keeps a system useful as well as careful.

No retrospective change of a registered test.

These are corrections to this paper’s claims. Every frozen registration keeps its original text and decision rules. Any future test using the revised crossover or capacity interpretation requires its own prospective registration; a result cannot be relabelled by applying the new interpretation after it was observed.

Standing covenant.

Prove this paper wrong, and I will publish the refutation myself. Falsification conditions are stated in this paper; the standing challenge: github.com/MichaelDariusEastwood/arc-scaling-challenge.

8 What this paper does and does not show

The contribution is a cross-domain framework within the ARC Theory and Recursive Dynamics: conditional mathematical results, explicit limits, and a prospective test of whether composition information improves scaling predictions. The classical functional-equation families are established mathematics. Their application to a particular recursive system requires a separate argument. The cumulative-advantage ODE supplies a shifted power law and an asymptotic exponent on its stated premises; it does not make those premises true of an AI, organism or physical device.

The empirical standing.

The March 2026 runs are precursor evidence that decides no registered proposition (Section 4.3). A sequential advantage was observed only where both exponents could be estimated, while Gu et al. (2026) report the opposite direction in their comparison. The one interpretable error-suppression fit is inconclusive; its metric is defined in Section 3.1. The alignment comparison cannot decide F13 (Section 6.5). These observations do not validate the exponent identity, a crossover criterion or a universal ceiling. The mathematical corrections in this revision are evaluated through their assumptions and proofs, separately from those measurements.

Status, as at 1 November 2026.

What this programme names laws are conjectures. Laws I to III were registered on 8 September 2026 and Laws IV and V on 15 October 2026 (version 1.103), the mathematics of Laws IV and V still in development (version 1.2, 29 October 2026). Each is a law under test: Law IV has not yet been tested, and the counted test of Law V’s placement limb is Unit 83, below. The theory registration of twenty-two propositions was registered on 8 September 2026 at version 1.100 and updated on 13 September 2026 (version 1.102), 15 October 2026 (version 1.103) and 29 October 2026 (version 1.104, which adds no prediction and changes no law’s statement); its terms are defined in a separate register. The first registered study, Unit 06, a classification audit that tests no law, was submitted for registration on 1 October 2026, shown approved and public on 4 October 2026, and ran on 6 October 2026; one of its two runs could not start, so it is reported in full as administratively incomplete, with no inferential verdict. A second, Unit 83, the counted test of P21 under Law V, has an OSF registration created on 22 October 2026 and public from 25 October 2026, and ran on 27 and 28 October 2026: P21 is supported under the registered test, by the programme’s own run, on the access axis, family-dependent, with its mechanism axis not evaluable and one call retried under a disclosed recovery amendment (results: DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/98HKR). Two different axes are named here. The access axis is what Unit 83 varied: both reviewers are called each round, but the corrector sees the earlier kept entries with a marked new arrival and may revise it, while the monitor sees its accumulated register with the new arrival unmarked and can only accept or reject it. The performance axis is what it measured, the outcome, as against the mechanism axis, which was not evaluable. Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, remains a law under test: its placement limb, P21, is supported on the performance axis only, with its mechanism axis not evaluable, which is not support for the information-asymmetry mechanism; its build-order limb, read on P12, is undecided, since P12 is untested. A third, Unit 82, the counted test of P17, the premise beneath Law III’s value two (Section 6.4), was registered on OSF on 27 October 2026 and has not yet run. The trials that would decide this paper’s own predictions are drafts awaiting the author’s submission. Every quantity in the formal model is defined in Appendix D and given a measurement in Appendix E, some in working definitions not yet tested, and established-law standing is claimed nowhere. The registered programme exists to earn that standing, or lose it, by measurement, replication and survived refutation.

9 Limitations

Evidential limitations.

The earlier estimate of about 2.2 is retracted, and the one interpretable fit of the v5 cross-architecture experiment, Gemini 3 Flash’s, is what survived it, one model’s fit and inconclusive, not a correction of the same measurement (Section 4.3); the five capability runs of March 2026 are precursor evidence that decides no registered proposition. No α\alpha has been measured in time crystals. The COGITATE connection is structural, not quantitative. The βL\beta_L-to-α\alpha relationship is an identity proved in Appendix A.2 and checked numerically (R2=1.00000000R^2 = 1.00000000), an internal consistency check and not a validation of the relation in any system; the empirical measurement of βL\beta_L in physical systems requires independent confirmation. The R*R^* crossover is untested empirically. The former numerical βL\beta_L bands have no established phase-boundary interpretation; Section 5.4 separates the ODE parameters from the functional-equation premises. Conjecture 5 (⊕\oplus transitions) has descriptive local-estimate checks in three computational systems, beside a Bernoulli control (Appendix F.6), and untested in physical experiments. The five-property test (Theorem 4) did not reach statistical significance (p=0.095p = 0.095) and requires larger samples. The alignment run of March 2026, a single unregistered run, cannot decide criterion F13: its statistics are rank correlations and contrasts, not exponents, and its three flat and negative runs are the three the October 2026 code review found defective (Section 6.5).

Blind prediction testing.

A blind prediction test was conducted on three computational systems (Barabási-Albert networks, gradient descent with momentum, Kuramoto oscillators). The measured α\alpha values were 3 to 20×20\times smaller than predicted by α=1/(1−βL)\alpha = 1/(1-\beta_L). However, forensic analysis identified two independent confounds: (1) the numerical-derivative βL\beta_L estimation method is fatally biased, giving βL≈0.95\beta_L \approx 0.95 regardless of true βL\beta_L, even for pure Bernoulli systems with 3 per cent Gaussian noise added; (2) none of the tested systems satisfy Axiom 2 (constant coupling coefficient aa), and the BA network’s effective coupling decreases ∼50×\sim 50\times over the simulation. Applied to systems built to satisfy Axiom 2, the linearisation method recovers the relation with R2=0.9999R^2 = 0.9999, which checks the method, not the prediction for the three systems tested. The prospective predictions failed on those systems. The subsequent diagnostics can explain why that design was not a clean test of the conditional identity; they do not make the predictions successful. A new blind test with the method fixed in advance is required, and identifying natural systems that satisfy the axioms remains the central empirical challenge. Full methodology and forensic analysis are available as supplementary material (see Paper III).

Theoretical limitations.

The framework formalises the pattern of recursive amplification but does not identify the mechanism. Theorem 2 is the solution of the growth equation Axiom 2 assumes, and Theorem 2a follows from the product form Axiom 1 assumes; their weight lies in what they make measurable, and the axioms themselves are untested in any physical system. It tells you what happens (scaling exponents, crossover depths, functional forms) but not why at a microscopic level (analogous to thermodynamics before statistical mechanics). Connecting the composition operator to microscopic dynamics remains an open problem.

10 Conclusion

The central question is whether a description of how gains combine can predict a later scaling curve. The paper supplies conditional mathematical results and a prospective way to test their usefulness. Cauchy’s equations constrain families under stated hypotheses; the cumulative-advantage ODE gives a shifted power law, an asymptotic exponent and a coordinate-dependent characteristic scale. Neither a fixed update rule nor frozen model weights fixes an empirical exponent.

Every system discussed in this paper (silicon neural networks, superconducting qubits, millimetre polymer beads, cortical neural circuits) maintains a low-entropy state far from equilibrium and, on this paper’s reading, feeds its outputs back into its inputs. Under the cumulative-advantage model their gains would change smoothly from approximately linear towards compounding over a characteristic scale of depth (Theorem 3), universal in structure and domain-specific in form on the framework’s premises; no such scale has yet been measured in any of them (criterion F7).

The present record does not establish a universal law across domains. The AI error-suppression estimate is inconclusive. The biological comparisons require distinct observables and independent dimension assignments. The physical analogies and exact reference relations motivate questions without validating the proposed common mechanism. Unit 83 supplies a qualified result for its own correction-placement contrast, with the full limits in Section 8; it decides none of this paper’s scaling or ceiling claims.

The ARC Ceiling remains a law under test whose conditional premises are stated in Section 6.4. A declining error fraction, an absolute error burden and growth in elapsed time are different questions. No safety guarantee follows from a fitted exponent. The next contribution should be a locked prediction that succeeds or fails on held-out trajectories against serious alternatives, with the outcome published either way.

If the predictions fail, we will have learned where the structural analogy breaks down. If they hold, we will have identified a principle that connects intelligence, computation, and the physics of order across substrates. Intelligence may not be a property of particular materials. It may be what happens where recursion compounds its own gains, a hypothesis this paper states and does not establish.

Conjectural extrapolation.

The furthest reading of the framework comes last, as a conclusion the mathematics does not deny rather than a result: Law I, a law under test, taken to the limit of capability does not rule out a universe or its creation. Established physics asks about both in its own terms. On the universe’s settings, Steven Weinberg wrote: “Astronomical observations indicate that the cosmological constant is many orders of magnitude smaller than estimated in modern theories of elementary particles” (Weinberg 1989). On the formation of a new universe, Blau, Guendelman and Guth found that, for a range of initial conditions, a region of false vacuum inflates, and that “an observer in the interior will describe a closed universe which completely disconnects from the original spacetime” (Blau et al. 1987). Neither work concerns intelligence or this framework, and neither supports the reading. No measurement in this paper bears on that reading, no prediction of it is registered, and no test of it is in view, so it is graded as conjecture and is not established. Its premise is testable: the reading needs the framework to hold beyond AI, and the forward prediction of Section 6.1 (registered as P18) and criterion F10 test whether the composition description predicts held-out scaling in other systems; their failure would remove that premise. The reading belongs to the long-horizon interpretive layer of Infinite Architects (Eastwood 2026f), requires independent argument and evidence beyond what is reported here, and is a reason for nothing else in this paper.

The predictions are specified. The falsification criteria are public. The data will decide.

Code and data.

The paper’s figures and results files are in the folder papers/Foundational of the public repository github.com/MichaelDariusEastwood/arc-principle-validation, and the scripts and results of the computational checks of Appendix F are in its folders experiments/domain-validation__Foundational-and-Origin and experiments/blind-prediction-test__Paper-III-and-Foundational, cited at commit 427b897d. Two of the deposited results files in the paper’s folder, results_arc_1d_prediction_test.txt and results_complete_suite.txt, credit the saprotrophic fungal rows to a study of 1975 and give a temperature of 25 degrees Celsius; the source Section 6.4 reads, Aguilar-Trigueros et al. (2017), credits those rows in its Table 1 to a study of 2013 and gives 28 degrees, and the files are kept as deposited. The paper and its earlier versions are deposited at doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/Y7QGD.

A Proofs

A.1 Proof of Theorem 1 (classification)

Case 1: multiplicative composition.

Proof. Hypothesis: g:ℝ+→ℝ+g: \mathbb{R}^+ \to \mathbb{R}^+ continuous with g(1)=1g(1) = 1 and g(R1⋅R2)=g(R1)⋅g(R2)g(R_1 \cdot R_2) = g(R_1) \cdot g(R_2).

Define h(x)=ln⁡g(ex)h(x) = \ln g(e^x). Then: h(x+y)=ln⁡g(ex+y)=ln⁡g(ex⋅ey)=ln⁡[g(ex)⋅g(ey)]=h(x)+h(y)\begin{equation*} h(x + y) = \ln g(e^{x+y}) = \ln g(e^x \cdot e^y) = \ln[g(e^x) \cdot g(e^y)] = h(x) + h(y) \end{equation*}(A.1) This is Cauchy’s additive functional equation. Under the continuity of gg (hence hh), every solution has the form h(x)=αxh(x)=\alpha x for a constant α\alpha; monotonicity makes α≥0\alpha\geq0. Therefore ln⁡g(ex)=αx\ln g(e^x) = \alpha x, giving g(R)=Rαg(R) = R^{\alpha}. ◻

Case 2: additive composition.

Proof. Hypothesis: f:[0,∞)→ℝ+f: [0, \infty) \to \mathbb{R}^+ continuous with f(0)=1f(0) = 1 and f(r1+r2)=f(r1)⋅f(r2)f(r_1 + r_2) = f(r_1) \cdot f(r_2), in the added passes r=R−1r = R - 1.

Taking logarithms: ln⁡f(r1+r2)=ln⁡f(r1)+ln⁡f(r2)\ln f(r_1 + r_2) = \ln f(r_1) + \ln f(r_2). This is again Cauchy’s additive equation, whose continuous solutions have the form ln⁡f(r)=αr\ln f(r)=\alpha r, with α≥0\alpha\geq0 under monotonicity, giving f(r)=eαrf(r) = e^{\alpha r}, so that g(R)=f(R−1)=eα(R−1)g(R) = f(R - 1) = e^{\alpha(R-1)} and g(1)=1g(1) = 1, as Axiom 1 requires. ◻

Case 3: bounded composition.

Proof. Qr+1=min⁡(Qr+δQr,Qmax)Q_{r+1} = \min(Q_r + \delta Q_r,\, Q_{\max}). For any monotonically increasing sequence {Qr}\{Q_r\} bounded above by QmaxQ_{\max}, lim⁡r→∞Qr≤Qmax\lim_{r \to \infty} Q_r \leq Q_{\max}. Therefore f(R)=Q(R)/If(R) = Q(R)/I is bounded and converges to a limit no greater than Qmax/IQ_{\max}/I: UU saturates, at the ceiling only if the increments sum to at least the remaining gap, equality sufficing for attainment in the limit. ◻

A.2 Proof of Theorem 2 (scaling exponent)

Proof. From Axiom 2: dg/dr=agβLdg/dr = ag^{\beta_L}, βL∈[0,1)\beta_L \in [0,1), g(0)=1g(0) = 1, with r=R−1r = R - 1 the passes after the first. Separating variables: ∫1gs−βLds=∫0radr\begin{equation*} \int_1^{g} s^{-\beta_L}\, ds = \int_0^{r} a\, dr \end{equation*}(A.2) g1−βL−11−βL=ar\begin{equation*} \frac{g^{1-\beta_L} - 1}{1-\beta_L} = ar \end{equation*}(A.3) g(r)=[1+(1−βL)ar]1/(1−βL)\begin{equation*} g(r) = \left[ 1 + (1-\beta_L)ar \right]^{1/(1-\beta_L)} \end{equation*}(A.4) At fixed parameters, as r→∞r\to\infty, g(r)∼[(1−βL)ar]1/(1−βL).g(r)\sim[(1-\beta_L)ar]^{1/(1-\beta_L)}. The asymptotic exponent is therefore α=1/(1−βL)\alpha=1/(1-\beta_L). Since R=r+1R=r+1, the same asymptotic exponent holds in RR. Exact equality g(R)=Rαg(R)=R^\alpha at every R≥1R\geq1 requires (1−βL)a=1(1-\beta_L)a=1, equivalently a=αa=\alpha. ◻

A.3 Proof of Theorem 3 (characteristic scale)

Proof. Write c=α/a=R*>0c=\alpha/a=R^*>0 and g(r)=(1+r/c)αg(r)=(1+r/c)^\alpha. Taylor expansion at fixed parameters gives g(r)=1+ar+βLa2r2/2+O(r3)g(r)=1+ar+\beta_La^2r^2/2+O(r^3). Dividing by (r/c)α(r/c)^\alpha gives a ratio tending to one as r→∞r\to\infty.

For r>0r>0, differentiation gives dlog⁡gdlog⁡r=αrr+c.\frac{d\log g}{d\log r}=\frac{\alpha r}{r+c}. This equals α/2\alpha/2 at r=cr=c, and equals qαq\alpha at r=qc/(1−q)r=qc/(1-q) for 0<q<10<q<1. If α>1\alpha>1, it exceeds one exactly when r>c/(α−1)=1/(aβL)r>c/(\alpha-1)=1/(a\beta_L). If βL=0\beta_L=0, g(r)=1+arg(r)=1+ar is linear. In the first-pass coordinate the elasticity is instead αR/(R−1+c)\alpha R/(R-1+c).

The scale contains no II when aa and βL\beta_L are held fixed. No claim that a real input-quality change preserves those parameters follows from this algebra. Finally, with ϵ=1−βL\epsilon=1-\beta_L, log⁡(g)=log⁡(1+ϵar)/ϵ→ar\log(g)=\log(1+\epsilon ar)/\epsilon\to ar as ϵ→0\epsilon\to0 at fixed a,ra,r, proving the finite-depth exponential limit. ◻

A.4 Why Axiom 2 takes this form

Why dg/dr=agβLdg/dr = ag^{\beta_L} and not some other functional form? This is the Bernoulli-type ODE for cumulative advantage (Price 1976), known in network science as preferential attachment, applied to the amplification factor gg rather than absolute capability. The exponent βL\beta_L parameterises the degree of self-reference: βL=0\beta_L = 0 gives constant growth (no feedback); βL→1\beta_L\to1 gives an exponential limit at fixed aa and finite rr. The choice βL∈[0,1)\beta_L \in [0,1) is the minimal model for a system where accumulated amplification accelerates future gains without divergence at finite RR. More complex models (e.g., dg/dr=agβL−bgνdg/dr = ag^{\beta_L} - bg^{\nu}, with ν\nu a damping exponent) would introduce additional parameters; we adopt the minimal form and test it against observation.

Author’s Note: Mathematical Corrections

This version incorporates the following corrections to the broader framework. These papers have not undergone formal human peer review; the author’s statement on tool assistance is in the declaration at the end of this paper.

1. Axiom 2 Correction:

The Cumulative Advantage ODE now operates on the amplification factor g(R)g(R) with g(0)=1g(0) = 1, matching Paper III. Previous versions applied the ODE to accumulated capability QQ with Q(0)=IQ(0) = I, which coupled the base potential II into the recursive dynamics and violated the separability asserted in Axiom 1 (U=I×g(R)U = I \times g(R)). The corrected formulation yields the simpler crossover formula R*=α/aR^* = \alpha/a, independent of II.

2. Quadratic Limit Regrounding:

The derivation of α≤2\alpha \leq 2 from stability analysis, elasticity, and Lyapunov/edge-of-chaos arguments has been withdrawn as these arguments contained category errors (elasticity >1> 1 does not imply dynamical instability; an autonomous flow on the line is monotone, so it cannot so much as oscillate, still less turn chaotic, and in two dimensions the Poincaré-Bendixson theorem shuts chaos out as well). The corrected justification is information-theoretic: transformer self-attention creates at most O(N2)O(N^2) pairwise information pathways, imposing a quadratic ceiling on information density per recursive step. Counting pathways this way is a heuristic and proves nothing about capability, and the move from quadratic pathway density to β=1/2\beta = 1/2 is a further conjecture, as is the supposition that any of it carries across to classical sequential systems at large. What now supports the value two in the theory is the pacing derivation of Law III at γ=1/2\gamma = 1/2, given in correction 9 below and in the statement paper.

3. Kleiber Reframing:

Kleiber’s Law (M0.75M^{0.75}, implying α≈1.33\alpha \approx 1.33) is now explained through thermodynamic drag, the physical costs of pumping fluids through three-dimensional fractal networks, dissipating heat, and distributing resources against gravity, rather than as a geometric constraint preventing a stability-limited maximum. The formula α=d/(d+1)\alpha = d/(d+1) itself has been independently derived by multiple groups (West et al. 1997, 2004; Banavar et al. 1999; Demetrius 2008; Zhao 2022; Bettencourt 2013); the ARC framework’s contribution is identifying Cauchy-constrained recursive composition as the reason these independent derivations converge. Demetrius and Tuszynski (2010) independently derived the same formula from quantum oscillator coupling, producing identical predictions.

4. Epistemic Status:

The equation Umax=I×R2U_{\max} = I \times R^2 is offered as a conjecture rather than a result, and the limit it sets on classical sequential computation is relative to architecture: an architecture-relative capacity ceiling of the kind information theory supplies, not a physical stability law.

These refinements preserve all core predictions: the β\beta-to-α\alpha derivation, the five structural properties, the composition operator classification, and the falsification criteria remain unchanged (a thirteenth criterion, F13, on alignment scaling, is introduced in Paper III).

5. v3.0 Additions:

This version adds the Six Hidden Assumptions of Cauchy’s classification (§2.2), the Hyers-Ulam stability theorem (Hyers 1941; Ulam 1960) establishing that each of the recognised scaling forms is stable within its own equation (a function approximately satisfying one of Cauchy’s equations lies near an exact solution of that same equation), the Attractor Theorem combining these results with the β\beta-derivation, and a structural implication connecting the composition operator classification to the space of possible classical scaling laws (§4.4). The earlier framing of the three forms as “stable attractors in function space” is withdrawn: the stability is per-equation, not a partition of function space, because a function satisfying none of the equations is not drawn toward any of them.

6. v3.1 Additions (March 2026):

This update integrates empirical results from the v5 cross-architecture experiment (Paper II), which tested 6 frontier AI models (Grok 4.1 Fast, Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4, DeepSeek V3.2, Gemini 3 Flash, Groq Qwen3) on 30 problems with bootstrap confidence intervals. Key findings: (a) sequential advantage is universal (αseq>αpar\alpha_{\text{seq}} > \alpha_{\text{par}} for every model), (b) the best-fitting power law, on Gemini 3 Flash, is one model’s fit and inconclusive, its sequential point estimates positive but sub-linear (§3.3 prints its row whole), (c) the scaling exponent is architecture-dependent, ranging from near-zero to ∼3\sim 3, and (d) the quadratic bound conjecture (α≤2\alpha \leq 2) is neither confirmed nor refuted. Alignment scaling results from Paper IV are also integrated: αalign\alpha_{\text{align}} is architecture-dependent, ranging from −0.25-0.25 (Gemini) to +0.44+0.44 (Claude Opus 4.6), with a three-tier hierarchy. These findings preserve the mathematical framework while significantly revising the empirical predictions for AI systems. Sections updated: §3, §4.1, §5, §6, §7, §8.

7. v4.0 Additions (March 2026):

Brief note on the Eden Protocol’s first in-programme empirical pilot (§5.5). No changes to the mathematical framework.

8. v5.0 Corrections (24 March 2026):

Four corrections identified by review. (1) The d=2 biological prediction (jellyfish/cnidarians) is reclassified from ‘confirmed’ to ‘unconfirmed’ pending identification of a valid test organism with genuinely two-dimensional resource transport. The Friedmann cosmological confirmation at d=2 is retained. (2) The d=3 mammalian exponent is acknowledged as debated (0.67 to 0.75 range), with the framework predicting this variation rather than a single universal value. (3) The derivation of α=d/(d+1)\alpha = d/(d+1) is clarified to require three conditions (multiplicative composition, space-filling geometry, and a conservation or optimisation constraint), not space-filling alone. (4) Demetrius and Tuszynski (2010) added as an independent derivation from quantum oscillator coupling. No changes to the mathematical framework or core predictions.

9. Stability Ceiling Correction (16 August 2026):

The ceiling was printed as αcrit=1/γ\alpha_{\text{crit}} = 1/\gamma. Under this paper’s own definition of γ\gamma that form runs the wrong way: it makes a better corrector lower the ceiling, and the same-class cap γ≤1/2\gamma \le 1/2 would give a ceiling of at least two rather than at most two. The corrected form is αcrit=1/(1−γ)\alpha_{\text{crit}} = 1/(1-\gamma), the reciprocal of the corrector’s shortfall from full proportionality, obtained from the pacing condition αγ>α−1\alpha\gamma > \alpha - 1. At γ=1/2\gamma = 1/2 both forms return two, which is why the error survived review; a discrimination study at values away from one half, where the two families separate, is drafted and awaits human submission. The superseded form is retracted and entered in the corrections log.

10. Physics Aggregate Withdrawn (14 August 2026):

The previously reported below-0.2 per cent mean error across physics domains is withdrawn. A mean taken over analytic identities is not a measurement of predictive accuracy. The individual domain entries stand on their own terms; the aggregate does not, and it is not restored in weakened form.

11. Earthquake Datum Withdrawn (14 August 2026):

The earthquake B-value row is a definitional identity rather than an independent measurement of the exponent, and is removed from the physics comparison and its figures. It is retained separately as a variable-pair case study, where it is informative about the method rather than about the prediction.

12. Hyers-Ulam Scope Narrowed (14 August 2026):

The statement that the three scaling forms are stable attractors in function space is withdrawn. Hyers-Ulam stability is per-equation: a function approximately satisfying one of the functional equations lies near an exact solution of that same equation, and a function satisfying none of them is not drawn toward any. The formal stability statement is preserved; the ubiquity implication is separated as a distinct empirical question that Hyers-Ulam alone does not settle.

13. Body Reconciled With Corrections 10 and 11 (1 September 2026):

Corrections 10 and 11 withdrew the earthquake B-value row and the sub-0.2 per cent mean, yet both survived in the section 5.4 physics table and in the sentence that summarised it. Neither appears in the body any longer: each of the four instances that remain is assessed on its own merits, and no aggregate figure is stated.

14. Theorem 1’s Premises Separated (19 September 2026):

The theorem’s header binds all three cases to Axioms 1 to 3. Under this paper’s own definitions that header is wider than the results need. Solved in the clock Axiom 2 declares, the axiom gives g(R)=[1+(a/α)(R−1)]αg(R) = [1 + (a/\alpha)(R-1)]^{\alpha} for R≥1R \geq 1. Case (1)’s pure power agrees with that solution only where a=αa = \alpha; case (2)’s exponential would require β=1\beta = 1, which the axiom’s declared domain β∈[0,1)\beta \in [0,1) excludes; and case (3) never saturates under it, because the solution is unbounded for a>0a > 0 and α>0\alpha > 0. The corrected statement is that cases (1) and (2) rest on Axiom 1, Axiom 3 and each case’s own composition hypothesis, exactly as Appendix A.1 proves them, with Axiom 2 not among their premises; and that case (3) rests on the capped recurrence it states, its ceiling remaining separable from base potential only if the ceiling is itself proportional to base potential. All three results stand as printed. The Cauchy classification needs no differential equation, and Theorem 2’s relation α=1/(1−β)\alpha = 1/(1-\beta) falls out of the case (1) check unchanged.

15. The Declared Clock Carried Into the Solution (19 September 2026):

Axiom 2 declares the added-recursion clock r=R−1r = R - 1, so that g=1g = 1 at r=0r = 0 restates Axiom 1’s g(1)=1g(1) = 1. The solution is then printed with RR standing in for rr at Theorem 2, at Theorem 3 and twice in Appendix A, and Appendix A.2’s integral in drdr carries an upper limit of RR. Evaluated at the declared baseline, the printed form returns [1+a/α]α[1 + a/\alpha]^{\alpha}, which exceeds one for every admissible rate constant where the axiom requires one. The corrected statement is that the solution in the declared clock is g=[1+(a/α)r]αg = [1 + (a/\alpha)r]^{\alpha} for r≥0r \geq 0, equivalently g(R)=[1+(a/α)(R−1)]αg(R) = [1 + (a/\alpha)(R-1)]^{\alpha} for R≥1R \geq 1, and that each equation should say which clock it counts in; the zero-depth reading beneath Theorem 2a is to be taken in the declared clock, where zero added passes is the first pass. The consequence for the crossover is a shift by one and nothing else: α/a\alpha/a is the crossover measured in added passes, and the same depth counted from the first pass is 1+α/a1 + \alpha/a. Theorem 2a is otherwise untouched: run with the declared clock’s baseline throughout, its contradiction still stands, so the theorem is sound and its symbols alone were wrong. The repair made at Axiom 2 in v5.14 is real and is not reopened here; what this correction reaches is the places downstream of it.

16. Theorem 4’s Properties and Their Premises (19 September 2026):

The theorem states that all five properties follow from Axioms 1 to 3 alone, regardless of which composition operator applies, and the conclusion repeats that they follow as theorems and not as empirical generalisations. Two of the five carry more than the axioms. Property 4’s exact doubling law, that doubling recursive depth multiplies capability by 2α2^{\alpha} at any base potential, holds only where a=αa = \alpha, the condition correction 14 records; under bounded composition it fails outright, because iterating it grows without bound against a finite ceiling, so the phrase regardless of which composition operator applies is false as printed. Property 5 is justified in its own sentence by finite energy and external error mechanisms, and neither appears anywhere in the three axioms. The corrected statement is that property 3 and the base-quality half of property 4 follow from Axiom 1 alone; that property 1 follows from Axioms 1 to 3 through Theorem 3, as the property’s own justification states; that the exact 2α2^{\alpha} doubling holds in the pure-power case and asymptotically otherwise; and that property 5 rests on a named added premise about finite resources and external error. What is preserved unweakened is the conjunction of the five as the framework’s distinctive prediction, the observation that the conjunction is what is uncommon, and the falsification criterion that a system with four of the five but not the fifth would constrain the framework.

17. Convexity Holds at Every Depth (19 September 2026):

Property 2 states that capability is strictly increasing and convex above the crossover, and justifies it by g(R)=Rαg(R) = R^{\alpha} being convex for α>1\alpha > 1. Differentiating Axiom 2 directly gives d2g/dr2=a2βg2β−1d^{2}g/dr^{2} = a^{2}\beta g^{2\beta-1}, which is strictly positive at every depth for a>0a > 0 and β>0\beta > 0, and zero at β=0\beta = 0. The printed sentence is therefore true and weaker than the truth, and the justification quoted for it reads the asymptotic pure power rather than the solution of the axiom. The corrected statement is that amplification is convex at every depth once the coupling is positive, and that R*R^{*} marks the depth at which compounding becomes numerically dominant rather than the depth at which curvature begins. The crossover is sited by the convention that the dimensionless argument is near one, which Appendix C.4 already names as an approximation carrying a 2 to 7 per cent error in the absolute value, so a claim that the transition is sharp needs a criterion of its own. What is preserved is R*R^{*} as a derived quantity, a function of the scaling exponent and the rate constant alone, independent of base potential, and checkable by measuring those two separately.

18. Case 3 Proves a Bound, Not Attainment (19 September 2026):

Appendix A.1 case 3 argues that a monotonically increasing sequence bounded above by the ceiling has a limit no greater than the ceiling, and concludes that capability saturates; Theorem 1 case (3) states the saturation value as the ceiling divided by base potential. The appendix proves the bound and not the value. A capped monotone process converges to a limit at or below the ceiling, and it reaches the ceiling only if the increments sum to at least the remaining gap, equality sufficing for attainment in the limit. The corrected statement is that the appendix establishes a limit no greater than the ceiling, and that the theorem’s value needs either the attainment condition stated beside it or the limit written as a bound. Requiring the partial sums to exceed the gap would be too strict, since the equality case attains the ceiling asymptotically: one overstatement is not to be replaced by another. What is preserved is that a capped monotone process converges, which is true and proved, and saturation as a qualitative regime.

19. The Crossover Does Not Move With Base Quality (19 September 2026):

The conclusion lists among the framework’s predictions a scaling crossover at a derived depth that shifts systematically with base quality. Five places in this paper say the opposite: correction 1 above, section 2.4, the falsification criterion at section 5.3, Appendix A.3, and Appendix C.4, which records that varying base potential does not shift the crossover. The derivation settles it in either clock, because base potential appears nowhere in Axiom 2 and nowhere in its solution, so α/a\alpha/a and 1+α/a1 + \alpha/a are both free of it. The provenance is on this page: correction 1 records that previous versions applied the equation to accumulated capability with base potential as the initial condition, which coupled base potential into the recursive dynamics, and under that superseded formulation a crossover moving with base quality was the correct prediction. The corrected statement is that the crossover is predicted to be independent of base quality and consistent across input qualities for a given architecture, matching Theorem 3, Appendix A.3, the falsification criterion and the computational validation. As with corrections 10 and 11 at correction 13, the defect is an earlier correction that did not reach the body. Every other prediction in that list stands unweakened: prediction of scaling behaviour from the composition operator alone, the coupling-to-exponent relation and its computational validation, the ARC Bound as a proposed stable-scaling limit with its architecture relativity and its expiring basis, and the composition operator transitions of Theorem 5.

Key findings that bear on the evidence presented in this section:
